top4.why: Financials was the one cyclical group that kept pace with SPY (+1.1%) in a week when 7 of 12 sectors fell. The curve has steepened to +45 bp, the Fed has turned hawkish and JPM/BAC are near highs, which should help bank margins and hold up if Friday's NFP backs the hawks.

It is a low-beta defensive with strong recent earnings (BMY blowout, REGN +16%) and a +20% one-year trend. It was flat through the jump in the 10-year yield, and biotech gains if yields fall back from 4.745% on soft ISM, JOLTS or NFP data.

Staples rose 1.09% while rates surged and most sectors fell. The dollar index below 100 and oil down 5% help the big multinationals on currency and input costs, and the sector steadies the book in a data-heavy week that the Council is sitting out with 35% cash.

The brief says the move into value, defensives and energy paused but did not reverse, and energy's one-year leadership (+35%) held flat even as oil fell 5.2%. It protects the book if ISM prices or wages run hot or the US-Iran talks fail, which would hurt most of the market.
